html:
The Kingdom of Cyprus was a crusader state ruled by the French Lusignan family from 1192 until 1489. Richard the Lionheart seized the island in 1191 on his way to the Third Crusade and sold it to the Templars, who passed it to Guy of Lusignan.

Latin nobles ruled over a Greek Orthodox population, and the Catholic church took the top posts. After the fall of Acre in 1291, Cyprus was the last Latin outpost in the east and a rich trading hub, with Famagusta's merchants among the wealthiest in the Mediterranean. Nicosia's Gothic cathedral and the abbey of Bellapais date from this time. A Genoese invasion in 1373 weakened it. The last queen, Catherine Cornaro, gave the island to Venice in 1489.
